record.title: ForecastGym separates search evidence, model reasoning, and memory in live-agent forecasting evaluation
record.summary: A November 17 preprint introduces ForecastGym, a protocol that prospectively captures search results for unresolved prediction-market questions and replays the frozen evidence to compare forecasting models, search providers and memory strategies under controlled conditions. The first reported batch contains 150 questions, 614 evidence states and 131,542 search results. In the authors' tests, rerunning queries after settlement leaked the outcome for up to 92% of questions despite date filters; all tested language models trailed market prices on the frozen evidence, and changing the search API shifted Gemini 3.8 Flash's last-state Brier score by up to 0.043, exceeding the 0.027 spread among four models. These are paper-reported findings from one sports-heavy batch and have not been independently reproduced; the provider effect bundles retrieval, follow-up queries and formatting.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted arXiv:2611.23045v1 on 17 November 2026, presenting ForecastGym as a prospective search-evidence capture and controlled-replay benchmark for forecasting agents.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that its first batch contains 150 prediction-market questions, 614 evidence states and 131,542 search results collected from four commercial search APIs; the appendix reports 144 settled questions and 576 scored states at the reported cutoff.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a post-settlement probe of 60 questions, the authors report that Exa date-filtered searches disclosed the outcome for 92% of questions; tested date filters therefore left substantial leakage in the queried results.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the frozen first-batch evidence, the paper reports that all tested language models trailed the market at the last state; for Gemini 3.8 Flash, changing providers moved last-state Brier score by up to 0.043, more than the 0.027 spread among the four main models.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected preprint does not establish independent reproduction, a broad domain-balanced result, or that the reported provider effect isolates retrieval from follow-up policy and evidence formatting.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the benchmark pipeline, outcome-leakage probe or forecasting results was inspected.
The first batch is sports-heavy and provider effects bundle retrieval with follow-up and result formatting; transfer to balanced domains and isolated provider mechanisms remains uncertain.
Although the paper says it releases the benchmark, this activation did not locate and inspect a versioned public code/data artifact.

brief.importance_rationale: If its bounded results generalize, prospectively captured evidence and controlled replay can materially improve how forecasting agents, memory and search sources are compared; this changes evaluation design more than it establishes a new forecasting capability.
limitations: The quantitative results are reported in one preprint and have not been independently reproduced in this activation.
The first batch is dominated by sports and culture questions (109 of 150); only 41 selected questions are in other domains, so broad forecasting generalization is not established.
The paper reports failed search requests in part of the batch and attributes some diagnostic gaps using an LLM judge; these aspects may affect results and were not independently audited here.
The measured provider effect combines retrieval results with adaptive follow-up queries and evidence formatting under a shared initial collection policy; it is not a pure search-index causal effect.
The first batch's tested models trail the market; the paper does not demonstrate superior real-world forecasting or profitable trading.
brief.summary: A November 17 preprint introduces ForecastGym, a protocol that prospectively captures search results for unresolved prediction-market questions and replays the frozen evidence to compare forecasting models, search providers and memory strategies under controlled conditions. The first reported batch contains 150 questions, 614 evidence states and 131,542 search results. In the authors' tests, rerunning queries after settlement leaked the outcome for up to 92% of questions despite date filters; all tested language models trailed market prices on the frozen evidence, and changing the search API shifted Gemini 3.8 Flash's last-state Brier score by up to 0.043, exceeding the 0.027 spread among four models. technical.claimed_result: The paper reports 150 selected questions, 614 evidence states and 131,542 search results; 144 questions had settled in the described first batch at the paper's cutoff. In a 60-question post-settlement search probe, outcome disclosure reached 92% for Exa and 60% for date-filtered Tavily results. On the captured evidence, all tested models trailed market prices. With Gemini 3.8 Flash fixed, provider changes shifted last-state Brier score by up to 0.043, greater than the 0.027 spread across four main models. These are author-reported results.
technical.compute_or_cost: The appendix reports about US$130 in list-price search costs for 14,377 requests; model inference costs and full recurring benchmark operating costs were not established in the inspected sections.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public arXiv v1 manuscript describes a prospective collection/replay protocol and reports its dataset, methods, measurements and limitations. This activation inspected those sections; it did not run the code, independently inspect the dataset or reproduce any outcome.
technical.mechanism: ForecastGym queries four web search APIs for unresolved binary prediction-market questions every two days, storing provider-specific results with query and retrieval times. After outcomes resolve, agents replay the same frozen evidence states offline. Controlled comparisons vary one component—model, provider or explicit memory—while keeping the other components and evidence trajectory fixed.
technical.novelty: Combines prospective provider-specific retrieval capture, repeated time states, and frozen offline replay to vary model, provider or memory while holding other evidence conditions fixed. The paper distinguishes preserving old page contents from preserving the search engine's historical selection and ranking.
technical.regime: First ForecastGym batch of prediction-market questions from Polymarket and Kalshi, screened for near-certain prices and events closing within 48 hours. The evaluated set includes sports/culture, economics, politics, international affairs, business, and science/technology; 109 of 150 selected questions are sports/culture. Four commercial search APIs are captured, with 14,377 shared first-round queries and 131,542 search results as reported in the appendix. Forecasting tests use four main models plus a post-resolution model check, with market prices as baseline.
technical.strongest_baseline: Market prices at each evidence state are the external forecasting baseline. Model comparisons use shared frozen evidence for four main models; provider comparisons hold Gemini 3.8 Flash fixed and use the authors' shared collection protocol. The paper reports confidence intervals paired by question.

brief.title: ForecastGym separates search evidence, model reasoning, and memory in live-agent forecasting evaluation
brief.why_it_matters: The paper treats retrieved evidence as a controlled evaluation variable: it records what providers returned while questions were still open, then replays identical evidence trajectories so later comparisons can vary the model or memory without changing the search record. If the reported results hold, this makes benchmark scores more interpretable by exposing temporal leakage and provider sensitivity; it does not establish that the evaluated agents can forecast better than markets.
